You should get a nice expression involving a0, a1, . . . , an−1 and t. Row expansion and induction is probably the best way to go. Problem 2. (i) Suppose A ∈ Mn×n(F ) is nilpotent i.e. there is an integer m > 0 such that Am = 0. Show that det(A) = 0. (ii) Show that if A ∈ Mn×n(F ) and c ∈ F , then det(cA) = cn det(A). (iii) Show that if A ∈ M(2n+1)×(2n+1)(R) is anti-symmetric then det(A) = 0. (iv) Suppose A ∈ Mn×n(R) is orthogonal i.e. AAt = I. Show that det(A) = ±1. (v) Suppose A ∈ M3×3(R) is orthogonal and det(A) = 1. Show that det(I − A) = 0. Hint: Show that At − I = (I − A)At and observe that At − I = −(I − A)t. Remark 1. (v) is saying that any rotation in R3 has an axis which is a nonzero vector in ker(I − A) or an eigenvector of A with eigenvalue 1. Problem 3. Let A ∈ Mn×n(R) be an invertible matrix with all entries being integers. Show that the entries of its inverse A−1 are all integers if and only if det(A) = ±1. Hint: Use the cofactor formula for A−1.
